question: The EU is seeing a rapid increase in cases of lumpy skin disease (LSD), which is seriously affecting livestock production and internal markets. In outbreaks detected in the Spanish province of Gerona, 2 500 cows had to be culled and the movement of 152 000 heads of livestock restricted, leading to immediate economic losses and serious concerns in the sector. In light of the above and given the risk of further cross-border spread: 1.
What is the Commission’s timeline for deploying an EU-wide LSD vaccine plan that will ensure priority supply, distribution and coverage in the most vulnerable areas?

What enhanced prevention and coordination measures will the Commission propose to prevent further outbreaks and contain the spread (controlling animal movement, vector surveillance, cross-border containment corridors/areas and good biosecurity practices on farms at risk)?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.2.2026) Within the EU framework for control measures and vaccination against lumpy skin disease (LSD)1 2 3 and in alignment with World Organisation for Animal Health standards4, emergency protective vaccination may be applied when epidemiologically justified.

Member States, not the Commission, decide whether to introduce vaccination for Category A diseases such as LSD and determine its scope and geographical extent in their national vaccination plans. The Commission coordinates Member States in outbreak management ensuring rapid regionalisation and adopting emergency measures protecting animal health.

It also provides scientific, technical and diagnostic support through the EU Reference Laboratory and the EU Veterinary Emergency Team and upon request, in emergency situations, rapid vaccine access from the EU vaccine bank. For additional details, the Commission would also like to refer to the answer to P004478/2025 and P-004548/2025/rev.15.
